sourceStatus: Daily Investment Brief still exposes client-side placeholders ('Analyzing...' / '--') to automated retrieval and no values are inferred. MacroMicro was unavailable in the latest verification cycle, so prior verified spread readings remain dated references only. Fresh dashboard changes are controlled by EIA, Federal Reserve/Treasury, FactSet, ECB, World Gold Council and current Reuters/MarketWatch reporting.
regime: The market is no longer well described by a simple risk-on/risk-off label. Physical scarcity and funded AI/power capex remain strong, but long-end yields, weak breadth and a heavier AI funding burden are increasing fragility. The main counterweight is still-positive earnings revision breadth. The investable distinction is funded cash-generative scarcity versus financing-dependent duration.

keyReadings.label: US 10Y after Treasury buyback announcement
keyReadings.note: Treasury announced up to $6bn of 10-20Y buybacks for Sep 10. Treat the yield response as a clearing-rate signal, not proof that buybacks cannot work.

keyReadings.label: US operable refining capacity
keyReadings.note: The dashboard uses limited spare refining slack, not the unsupported 'lowest capacity ever' claim.

channels.label: Growth / Demand
channels.interpretation: Services, earnings and power demand remain resilient, but energy inflation and high borrowing costs are weakening rate-sensitive and lower-quality demand.

channels.label: Policy Relief
channels.regime: Energy inflation leaves little room for relief
channels.interpretation: Oil/products and global gas pressure keep the near-term policy hurdle high ahead of PPI, CPI and the Fed.

channels.label: Financial Conditions
channels.interpretation: The 10Y rose to about 4.85% after Treasury announced larger long-end buybacks. Real yields remain restrictive and the long end is not behaving like a clean growth slowdown.

channels.label: Broad Credit
channels.regime: Open to quality, more expensive at the margin
channels.interpretation: High-quality markets remain open, but >$200bn of hyperscaler issuance and rising hyperscaler spreads increase the marginal cost of absorbing long-duration corporate supply.

channels.label: Weak-End Credit Stress
channels.regime: Weak borrowers remain the fault line
channels.interpretation: The prior verified CCC OAS remains elevated. The next escalation test is whether stress broadens into banks, consumer credit or otherwise healthy IG.

channels.label: Consumer
channels.interpretation: Record-near diesel, expensive gas in Europe and high borrowing costs reduce discretionary flexibility without yet proving a broad collapse.

channels.label: Housing
channels.interpretation: High 10Y/30Y yields keep mortgage and development economics restrictive.

channels.label: Industrial / AI / Power Capex
channels.regime: Physical demand record-strong, funding quality matters
channels.interpretation: EIA confirms record electricity demand from data centres and manufacturing. This channel stays strongly positive even while AI funding quality deteriorates.

channels.label: Input Costs
channels.regime: Energy, copper and logistics inflation overlap
channels.interpretation: Refined products, LNG, copper, freight and electrical inputs are all pressuring costs. Pricing power and pass-through remain decisive.

channels.label: Labour
channels.interpretation: Recent payroll resilience coexists with softer survey hiring.

channels.label: Risk Appetite
channels.interpretation: S&P/Nasdaq remain close to highs, but breadth, equal-weight and small caps are deteriorating under rising yields. Treat this as fragility, not a confirmed broad crash regime.

channels.label: Crude
channels.interpretation: Brent above $100 confirms the geopolitical premium; alternative routes and eventual Gulf normalization remain the medium-term counterweight.

channels.label: Refined Products
channels.interpretation: US refinery utilization reached 98% with elevated cracks and tight distillate inventories. The key signal is limited spare refining slack, not an all-history capacity low.

channels.label: US Gas
channels.regime: US balance moderate despite global LNG shock
channels.interpretation: Keep Henry Hub separate from global LNG. US gas is not as tight as Europe/Asia, so the existing stock-sensitivity channel should not inherit global LNG stress mechanically.

channels.label: Gold / Monetary Hedge
channels.regime: Strategic flows strengthening despite high real yields
channels.interpretation: August gold ETF inflows reached $18bn/121t and central-bank buying persists. Real yields remain the tactical timing gate.

channels.label: Copper / Industrial Metals
channels.regime: Scarcity/grid signal, not generic growth signal
channels.interpretation: Record copper validates grid/AI demand and mine scarcity, but soft China private-credit transmission means it should not be read as broad China reflation.

channels.label: Battery Storage / Lithium
channels.interpretation: Peak-load and grid needs support deployment while excess manufacturing keeps commodity cell/lithium economics selective.

channels.label: Agriculture / Fertilizer Inputs
channels.interpretation: Feedstock, freight and weather pressure support nitrogen/seed pricing but squeeze farm affordability.

channels.label: Equity Breadth
channels.interpretation: 383 S&P 500 names declined Sep 9; NYSE and Nasdaq breadth were strongly negative and the Russell 2000 is below its 50-day average. Diagnostic only: no automatic stock-score effect yet.

channels.label: Earnings Support
channels.interpretation: FactSet shows Q3 bottom-up EPS estimates rose 1.2% through July-August instead of the normal early-quarter decline. This is the main counterweight to weak breadth. Diagnostic only.

channels.label: AI Funding Quality
channels.interpretation: Hyperscaler debt issuance exceeds $200bn YTD and ECB evidence shows rising hyperscaler spreads. Keep this separate from the positive physical AI capex channel. Diagnostic only.

channels.label: Global LNG Availability
channels.interpretation: European gas is above €75/MWh with storage only around 66% and Middle Eastern LNG exports sharply reduced. This is a global inflation channel distinct from US Henry Hub. Diagnostic only.

dashboardGuardrails: Equity Breadth, Earnings Support, AI Funding Quality and Global LNG Availability are visible diagnostics only and have no stock macro-adjustment until explicit stock sensitivity factors are researched.
Creator option-wall levels, historical analogs, seasonality and single-stock chart patterns belong in Positioning/Tactical context, not Macro Pulse scoring.
Do not collapse US Gas and global LNG into one signal.
Do not interpret record copper as generic global-growth confirmation without China/physical-premium evidence.
Do not convert breadth deterioration into a crash regime without credit/earnings/price confirmation.
